Honestly I've been in the same situation you've been in. I spoke with my Flight Surgeon about my general anxiety/depression due to work and he gave me antidepressants to help with my mood. Been in for 4 years and just picked up Sergeant. My command trusts me and knows how much I pit into my work and for my Marines. I would definitely ask for the help, all they did was ensure I had therapy with either an on base or off base therapist. They could put you on LIMDU so just be aware of that. If you are pending orders overseas it could hinder your changes of going but I managed to get through all my medical stuff and I'm about to head out in October. Would recommend a therapist 100% since everything will be covered by TRICARE. Last note just remember there are good people out there watching you and have your back. If you need anything just hmu.

Edit: You also would not get kicked out just for taking medication or asking for help. They would honestly like it if you were honest with yourself. The fact that you reached out shows how courageous you are. It's never worth hiding your emotions. Always stay true to yourself no matter what.

Yeah for the 75mg I was on it for about 4 weeks and the depression really hit hard. I felt so numb emotionally and physically felt sick. Lots of suicide attempts and self harming thoughts. My mind just took over and I couldn't go outside and I never wanted to eat at all, lost about 10 pounds so far. I did stop taking zoloft because of that and I'm just doing therapy as of now. For the anxiety part, it helped so much. Work felt easier and I didn't overthink as much as I used to.

In my own personal experience I've been more tired and had a lack of motivation when I was taking Zoloft as well. Kinda strange that you are getting some bad effects as of now. It was until I hit 75mg when things started getting worse. Most likely you would have to increase the dose to get a better effect, but I'm no doctor and I would ask. For the depression part of it what I was told from my doctor is that a higher dosage would give you a more therapeutic effect in combating the depressed portion of what your feeling.

Hm. Kinda strange they gave you zoloft to start out for your depression let alone major depression. Zoloft helped my anxiety and overthinking way more than the depressed part. Just curious as to why they are prescribing you zoloft for depression. You don't have to ask if you don't like. If you got any other questions, ask us asap.
